items.question: How do I get started with PioSphere?
items.answer: Schedule a demo and our team will guide you through deployment on your own GPU infrastructure. Most teams are up and running within days, not months.

items.question: How does PioSphere compare to AWS, Azure, or GCP?

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How PioVation processes and protects personal data across its platform, services, and agreed customer deployments.

controller.title: Controller and contact
controller.intro: PioVation GmbH, Zehentmeierstraße 8a, 85630 Grasbrunn, Germany, registered at Amtsgericht München HRB 290989, VAT ID DE367131891, represented by its Managing Director Mazda Sabony, is the controller for the processing described in this policy.
items: Data protection contact: datenschutz@piovation.com.
This policy describes the technical and organisational measures pursuant to Article 32 GDPR that ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk when processing personal data.
It supplements, and does not replace, the applicable data processing agreement and the confidentiality and data protection undertaking of persons authorised to process data.

scope.title: Scope
scope.body: This policy applies to PioVation corporate systems, the platform and services, and agreed customer deployments. The specific applicability of individual measures depends on the agreed scope of services and the deployment model. For on-premise or private-cloud environments operated by the customer, responsibilities between PioVation and the customer are defined separately.

principles.title: Security principles
items: Need-to-know and least-privilege principle for access to systems and customer data.
Security by design and privacy by design in the development and operation of the platform.
Separation of production, test, and development environments, insofar as technically and organisationally required.
Risk-based selection, regular review, and continuous improvement of the security measures.
Clear responsibilities for information security, data protection, and incident response.

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality
confidentiality.intro: For the PioVation-hosted model, customer data is processed in Germany, operated in the EMC Home of Data data centre in Munich. The site is certified to ISO 27001, ISO 9001, and ISO 50001 and is built and operated in accordance with DIN EN 50600.
items: Physical access to PioVation's own premises is restricted to authorised persons; visitor access is controlled or accompanied in accordance with the relevant site rules.
Individual user accounts; shared administration accounts are avoided as far as possible.
Multi-factor authentication for privileged and security-critical access.
Role-based access control with authorisations assigned according to the least-privilege principle and reviewed regularly.
Logical separation of customer environments and workloads through suitable platform, network, project, or namespace isolation mechanisms.
Customer data is not made accessible to other customers.

integrity.title: Integrity
integrity.intro: Transmission and storage are protected according to the deployment model and protection requirement:
items: Encrypted transmission using state-of-the-art transport encryption (e.g. TLS).
Encryption of suitable storage media, volumes, databases, or backups depending on the deployment and protection requirement.
Access to cryptographic keys and secrets is restricted and managed in a traceable manner; secrets are not intentionally stored in source code.
Traceable software change processes, including version control and review procedures for security-relevant changes.
Dependencies, container images, and components are checked for known vulnerabilities on a risk basis; security updates are prioritised according to criticality.

Security-relevant administrative activities are logged insofar as technically possible and appropriate; logs are protected against unauthorised access and access to them is restricted to authorised roles.

availability.title: Availability and resilience
items: Monitoring of essential platform and infrastructure components.
Suitable backup and recovery procedures in accordance with the agreed service and deployment, with regular testing of the recoverability of critical data and systems.
Redundancy and failover concepts, insofar as they are part of the agreed service level.
Documented procedures for operational disruptions, escalation, and restart.
Capacity and resource monitoring for critical infrastructure components.

ai.title: AI-specific protective measures
ai.intro: Because the platform processes prompts, outputs, and model artefacts, additional safeguards apply:
items: Separation of prompts, outputs, model artefacts, and other customer data according to architecture and protection requirement.
Documented rules on whether and for what purposes inputs or outputs are stored.
No use of confidential customer content for general model training outside its purpose without a legal basis or contractual approval.
Restriction of access to model endpoints, inference APIs, model weights, and administrative functions.
Protection of API keys, tokens, and other credentials through suitable secret-management procedures.
When using external model or infrastructure providers, data flows, storage locations, and subprocessors are documented transparently.

incidents.title: Incident response and personal data breaches
items: Documented process for the detection, assessment, containment, and remediation of security incidents.
Defined internal escalation paths and responsibilities, with preservation of relevant logs and evidence.
In the event of a personal data breach, an immediate internal assessment is carried out.
Insofar as PioVation acts as a processor, the controller is supported or informed without undue delay in accordance with the contractual agreement.
After relevant incidents, a root-cause analysis and appropriate corrective measures are carried out.

deletion.title: Deletion, return, and data minimisation
items: Personal data is processed only to the extent necessary for the respective purpose.
Appropriate retention and deletion rules are defined for production data, logs, temporary data, and backups.
After the end of the service, customer data is returned or deleted in accordance with the contract and instructions, insofar as no statutory retention obligations preclude this.
Backup copies may be removed from rotation cycles with a time delay; during this period they remain protected against production use and unauthorised access.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors and suppliers
subprocessors.body: PioVation assesses, on a risk basis, service providers that are essential for the processing or protection of customer data. For subprocessors, the agreements required under data protection law are concluded. The current list of approved subprocessors is maintained separately and made accessible to customers in accordance with the data processing agreement.

items: The customer defines the purposes of processing and assigns roles within its organisation.
The customer is responsible for the use of the platform within its sphere of control, including the management of its own credentials.
For on-premise and private-cloud environments operated by the customer, the customer provides the physical infrastructure, network, and perimeter protection as agreed.
The customer must not use the platform for unlawful purposes or in a way that impairs its availability for others.

dataProtection.title: Data protection
dataProtection.intro: Processing of personal data follows the applicable data processing agreement and the technical and organisational measures pursuant to Article 32 GDPR:
items: Confidential customer content is not used to train general models outside its purpose without a legal basis or contractual approval.

items: Essential platform and infrastructure components are monitored.
Backup and recovery procedures follow the agreed service and deployment, with regular restore testing.
Operational disruptions are handled through documented escalation and restart procedures.

about.subtitle: About
about.title: The cloud operating system for AI that stays on your infrastructure.
about.description: PioSphere unifies GPU infrastructure, LLM operations, and no-code AI agents into one platform - so enterprises, universities, and public agencies can run agentic AI entirely on their own terms.

story.label: Our story
story.title: Why we started PioVation
paragraphs: Most AI infrastructure today assumes an organization will hand over its data, its models, and its GPUs to somebody else's cloud. That trade-off doesn't sit well with enterprises, universities, and government agencies that carry real security and compliance obligations - so we built the alternative.

PioVation was founded in 2024 in Grasbrunn, working alongside AI researchers at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg. The mission the team set out with is a simple one: to make artificial intelligence accessible to everyone.

That mission became PioSphere - a cloud operating system built so any organization can stand up, manage, and audit its own AI agents, whether that means training a model on-premises, rolling out a no-code agent for a public agency, or offering agentic AI as a service to a cloud provider's own customers.

build.label: What we build
build.title: One platform, every layer
build.description: PioSphere is a full stack - from the GPUs sitting in your data center to the agents your teams use every day. Every layer can run on-premises, in the cloud, or split across both at once.

layers.title: AgentStudio & applications
layers.body: A no-code, drag-and-drop interface for designing, deploying, and iterating on AI agents - built for people who have never opened PyTorch or TensorFlow, and don't need to.

layers.title: PioSphere ACP - Agentic Cloud Platform
layers.body: LLM operations, agents, and retrieval, delivered as managed services: LLM Ops-as-a-Service, Agent-as-a-Service, and RAG-as-a-Service, each ready to plug into existing systems.

layers.title: PioSphere COS - Cloud Operating System
layers.body: Orchestration, access management, and the agent lifecycle - multi-tenant by design and equally at home in a lab, an on-premises data center, or a full regional deployment.

layers.title: Your infrastructure
layers.body: Any GPU, any vendor. Validated on AMD Instinct systems built by Supermicro and AMAX, so adopting PioSphere never means committing to one chipmaker or one cloud.

items.title: Sovereignty
items.body: PioSphere runs only in BSI-certified data centers in Germany, fully compliant with GDPR, with no dependency on US or Chinese cloud providers. For a public agency, that isn't a footnote - it's the whole point of calling us instead of someone else.

items.title: Openness
items.body: The platform is built to run on any GPU vendor's hardware, and has been validated on AMD Instinct systems from both Supermicro and AMAX. Choosing PioSphere never means locking in one chip or one rack.

items.title: Accessibility
items.body: AgentStudio turns agent-building into a drag-and-drop task, so the person closest to the problem can build the agent, instead of waiting in a queue behind an engineering team.

items.title: Control
items.body: Every agent is observable by default - token usage, behavior, and performance are logged and auditable, with role-based access control and policy enforcement built in from the start.

partners.label: Partners
partners.title: Built alongside
partners.description: PioSphere is co-developed and validated with hardware and research partners, not built in isolation.

architecture.subtitle: Architecture
architecture.title: How this documentation experience is built.
architecture.description: The API reference on /docs is embedded directly into the PioSphere frontend - no separate docs site, no iframe. This page walks through the layers, the data flow, and the tools behind it.

layers.label: Layers
layers.title: One app, four layers
layers.description: Each layer has a single job and talks only to its neighbors.

items.title: PioAgent service
items.body: The FastAPI backend defines the customer-facing API. Its OpenAPI schema is generated from the code itself, so the spec can never drift from the implementation.

items.title: GitHub Actions sync
items.body: A workflow exports the OpenAPI document from the service and commits it into this repository as docs/openapi.json. The spec travels through git like any other artifact - reviewable, versioned, revertible.

items.title: Vite + React bundle
items.body: The spec is imported at build time as a JSON module. No runtime fetch, no CORS, no flash of empty reference - the documentation ships inside the same bundle as the rest of the site.

items.title: Scalar reference
items.body: @scalar/api-reference-react renders the interactive reference: searchable sidebar, try-it requests, schema expansion. It is themed to follow the site's light/dark switch and offset to clear the fixed header.

flow.label: Data flow
flow.title: From code to page
flow.description: Five steps, fully automated after a change lands in the service repository.

steps.title: Route defined
steps.body: An endpoint is added or changed in the PioAgent service.

steps.title: Spec generated
steps.body: FastAPI emits the updated OpenAPI document.

steps.title: Action syncs
steps.body: GitHub Actions commits docs/openapi.json into the frontend repo.

steps.title: Bundle rebuilt
steps.body: Vite inlines the new spec into the next build of the site.

steps.title: Docs live
steps.body: The /docs reference reflects the change - same header, footer, and theme as every other page.

tools.label: Tools
tools.title: What it is built with
tools.description: Everything below runs in the frontend repository you are looking at.

items.name: React 19
items.body: The component model for the whole site, including the docs route.

items.name: Vite
items.body: Builds the app, resolves the OpenAPI JSON import, and serves everything on one origin.

items.name: TanStack Router
items.body: File-based routes; /docs and /architecture are ordinary routes in src/routes/.

items.name: Scalar
items.body: @scalar/api-reference-react renders the OpenAPI document as an interactive reference inside the React tree.

items.name: Tailwind CSS v4
items.body: Token-driven styling shared between the site chrome and the reference page.

items.name: react-i18next
items.body: English and German locales for every surface, including this page.

items.name: Framer Motion
items.body: Scroll-triggered reveals on this page, consistent with the about page.

items.name: FastAPI
items.body: The PioAgent backend whose generated OpenAPI schema feeds the reference.

items.name: GitHub Actions
items.body: Automates the path from service code to docs/openapi.json in this repo.
